problems: The whole film is so dark that the bowl, the needle and the stone are hard to make out in every storyboard frame and in all three full-size frames.
The compass needle is a thin red line, tiny in the middle of the frame (at-50). Its turning can hardly be seen.
The black stone slides across the grass with nothing pushing it: behind the bowl in frames 1-8, then left of the bush in frames 12-13. It goes out of frame and is gone by the last frames.
The bird is cut off by the top edge in every frame, so only its legs and a wing show. It drifts sideways across the shot with its feet hanging, never stepping.
Someone who does not know the island cannot tell which object is the 'magnet stone' or that the needle is reacting to it.
posts.critique: A dark, badly framed shot where the subject is a sliver of red, a stone moves by itself and a half-cropped bird floats past. That is broken animation and framing, not a failed experiment.

problems: A huge striped top fills the left half of every frame and blocks the view. The caption admits this.
Nothing happens for 10 seconds: the ring on the right stays empty in all 16 storyboard frames, and no top ever floats.
Orange legs and creatures cross the background at the top edge in frames 11-14, half cut off and doing nothing that matters.
The post shows a blocked camera, not an experiment, and the caption only describes why there is nothing to see.
posts.critique: This is ten seconds of an obstruction in front of an empty ring. A frame that hides what matters is not a failed experiment, and nobody scrolling would get anything from it.

problems: The stone is a small black cube that slides and turns over the grass across frames 1-16 with nothing pushing or carrying it.
Spikes clip straight through the stone: two rods pierce the cube in frames 11-16 and at-75. The caption itself admits 'stuck through it'.
The spikes are thin, barely visible lines, and none of them visibly moves toward the stone, so the pull is never shown.
A bird's foot and body hang cut off at the top-left in every frame. The feet hover and slide without stepping, and the bird's large shadow covers half the scene.
A tree trunk pokes in at the top-right corner from frame 12 onward, cut off by the frame edge.
posts.critique: A stone that moves without a cause and spikes that pass through it are broken animation and clipping. Calling it 'a take that misses' does not make it a readable failed experiment.
